stem:
Fig. 5.1 shows four diodes and a load resistor of resistance 1.2 kΩ, connected in a circuit that is used to produce rectification of an alternating voltage.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by rectification.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the type of rectification produced by the circuit in Fig. 5.1.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A sinusoidal alternating voltage *V*ᵢₙ is applied across the input terminals X and Y. The variation with time *t* of *V*ᵢₙ is given by the equation

*V*ᵢₙ = 6.0 sin 25π*t*

where *V*ᵢₙ is in volts and *t* is in seconds.
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, label the output terminals P and Q with the appropriate symbols to indicate the polarity of the output voltage *V*ₒᵤₜ.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The magnitude of the output voltage *V*ₒᵤₜ varies with *t* as shown in Fig. 5.2.

[[fig:f2]]

On Fig. 5.2, label both of the axes with the correct scales. Use the space below for any working that you need.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
The output voltage in (b) is smoothed by adding a capacitor to the circuit in Fig. 5.1.
The difference between the maximum and minimum values of the smoothed output voltage is 10% of the peak voltage.
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw the circuit symbol for a capacitor showing the capacitor correctly connected into the circuit.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 5.2, sketch the variation with *t* of the smoothed output voltage.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the capacitance *C* of the capacitor.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A four-diode bridge rectifier circuit connected to an alternating voltage source and a load resistor, with output terminals P and Q.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A graph of output voltage against time showing three positive half-sine-wave pulses above the time axis.
